**Finding: compliant (no redline).**

The agreement grants TrueLink no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against Mortgage Logic.com. This is better than the AUDIT preferred position — there is no frequency, notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, cost-allocation or system-access parameter to constrain because the underlying Vendor right does not exist.

Points confirmed in the investigation:
- **sec-8 (Client covenants)** — the planner's primary candidate — contains compliance, notification, access-restriction, credit-data licence, representation and spamming covenants only; no audit or records obligation. The single Client access obligation (p0060) requires Client to give TrueLink reasonable access to make Y2K repairs "at TrueLink's sole cost and expense" — remediation, not audit, and cost sits with the Vendor.
- **sec-5 / § 6** — the fee-verification mechanic runs in our favour: Client receives supporting documentation on request and may contest charges. No reciprocal TrueLink right to examine Client books or usage.
- **sec-10 (Confidentiality)** and the licence provisions contain no embedded inspection or verification right; § 2(e) again favours us (Client gets real-time usage statistics and raw log files).
- Regex sweeps for audit / inspect / records / books / verify / examine returned nothing; access-related hits were all inbound service-access or indemnity references.

No walk-away trigger (no unlimited, unannounced or remote-access audit) is present. Nothing to flag, and I have not upgraded the bargain to reach preferred wording since there is no responsive clause to edit.
